headline: Earnings surge as investment gains dwarf operating growth
summary_short: Berkshire's Q2 FY2026 net earnings reached $25,667M (+107.5% y/y), driven mainly by $12,684M of investment gains and the absence of last year's $3,760M Kraft Heinz impairment; core operating earnings rose a steadier 16.3% y/y to $12,983M.
summary_long: Revenue was $101,808M (+10.0% y/y, +8.7% q/q). Net earnings of $25,667M (+107.5% y/y) were dominated by $12,684M of investment gains and the absence of 2025's $3,760M Kraft Heinz impairment. Operating earnings, Berkshire's non-GAAP core measure, rose a steadier 16.3% y/y to $12,983M, led by manufacturing/service/retailing (+24%) and Berkshire Hathaway Energy (+27%), partly offset by weaker insurance-underwriting and insurance-investment income. Berkshire repurchased ~$4.5B of stock in the quarter; insurance float was ~$177.5B, up ~$1.1B since year-end 2025. Cash fell to $41,360M (-59.1% y/y); shareholders' equity rose to $747,910M (+12.0% y/y). No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Net earnings surge reflects $12,684M in investment gains (mostly unrealized equity mark-to-market) vs $4,970M a year ago, plus no repeat of 2025's $3,760M Kraft Heinz impairment; company calls such quarterly gains 'usually meaningless.'

Driven by larger investment gains and the absence of the prior-year Kraft Heinz other-than-temporary impairment; the release states investment gains/losses are 'not indicative of quarterly business performance.'
EPS tracks net earnings per share on a nearly flat Class B share count y/y, so it mirrors the same investment-gains and no-impairment drivers as net income.
Broadly consistent with $35,773M of six-month net earnings retained, partly offset by ~$4.8B of H1 buybacks disclosed by the company; other equity components not itemized in the release.
